hints: Focus on what each nitrogen oxide actually does once it is released from car engines and power stations.
Check statement 1 first, car exhaust $	ext{NO}$ is easily oxidised in air to $	ext{NO}_2$, a well known source of nitric acid in rain.
Now link $	ext{NO}_2$ to $	ext{SO}_2$ oxidation and to sunlight reactions with hydrocarbons, if all three links work then all three statements hold.
walkthrough:
**Recall where NOx comes from**

Think high temperature in internal combustion engines. Nitrogen and oxygen from air react to make $	ext{NO}$.

$$\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}$$

**Check statement 1, NO to acid rain**

$	ext{NO}$ is colourless but it is quickly oxidised in air to brown $	ext{NO}_2$.

$$2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$$
Then $	ext{NO}_2$ dissolves in rain water to give nitric acid and nitrous acid, so it is a direct cause of acid rain. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, NO2 helping to make sulfuric acid**

$	ext{NO}_2$ is a good oxidising agent. In the atmosphere it can oxidise $	ext{SO}_2$ to $	ext{SO}_3$ while itself being reduced back to $	ext{NO}$.

$$\text{NO}_2 + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO} + \text{SO}_3$$
Then the $	ext{SO}_3$ reacts with water:
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$
So $	ext{NO}_2$ promotes sulfuric acid acid rain even though the acid itself contains sulfur. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, photochemical smog**

In bright sunlight, nitrogen oxides, oxygen and unburnt hydrocarbons from petrol undergo a complex chain of reactions.
This forms photochemical smog containing ozone, $	ext{O}_3$, and peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN), both harmful pollutants. Statement 3 is correct.

**Conclude**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct descriptions, the combination for 1, 2 and 3 is the right choice.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Statement 1 describes NO oxidation to NO2 and nitric acid formation, statement 2 describes NO2 oxidising SO2 to SO3 leading to sulfuric acid, and statement 3 describes photochemical smog formation.
options.B: Incorrect, this combination includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3, but NOx plus hydrocarbons plus sunlight really does give photochemical smog with ozone and PAN.
options.C: Incorrect, this combination includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1, but NO is definitely oxidised to NO2 in air and NO2 definitely contributes to nitric acid rain.
options.D: Incorrect, this combination includes only statement 1. It wrongly rejects statements 2 and 3, but both are established atmospheric chemistry of nitrogen oxides.
